correctness.rationale: Compatible incidences use each tail vertex and each graph edge at most once as a matching pair. Any directed closed gradient path here uses the unique graph cycle; the two cyclic incidence faces each use all cycle vertices and edges, and cannot occur together. The cofaces of either cyclic simplex are exactly its join with the tail link. In that link the sole compatible pair is (u,v0u) with (w,uw); (u,uw) is isolated. The two closed stars intersect only inside the ordinary Morse complex, and each meets the ordinary Morse complex precisely in its boundary-simplex join with the link. Thus the geometric quotient splits as the wedge of the two relative quotients. Retracting the link edge to an endpoint gives a deformation of both joined spaces respecting the relative subspace. Afterward the pair is the suspension of the (n-1)-simplex and its boundary, an n-ball and its boundary, so each pointed quotient is S^n. Independently the relative groups for one block occupy degrees n-1,n,n+1 with ranks (1,3,1); the lower map is onto, the upper image is a primitive rank-one subgroup of the kernel, and the remaining generator has degree n. The inclusion is a simplicial cofibration, so its noncontractible cofiber rules out a homotopy equivalence. The one-edge comparison has a point link (and the published collapse). Inspected the frozen code and finite results for n=3 through 10, without executing the supplied script; the proof is uniform and does not rely on these cases.
